name: vwap_zscore_bounce_5s
author: adapted from claude-4.6-opus
thesis: Normalizing price deviation from VWAP into a z-score using rolling standard deviation creates a statistically grounded entry signal. When z-score of (price - VWAP) falls below -2.0 or rises above +2.0, the deviation is >2 sigma from the session mean — a statistically rare event that tends to snap back. The inefficiency exists because intraday price distributions are leptokurtic (fat-tailed) but mean-reverting within sessions, so extreme z-scores overshoot the true equilibrium. This edge is too small and labor-intensive for large funds but viable for retail with low fixed-cost brokerage.
mechanism: VWAP is the institutional execution benchmark. When spot deviates significantly from session VWAP, algorithmic execution engines increase order flow to mean-revert their fills toward VWAP. This creates measurable gravitational pull, especially during lower-volume mid-session periods when fewer competing flows are present.

exit.signal_exit: exit if vwap_zscore moves further against position (new extreme beyond -2.5 or +2.5)

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 24; reduce size 50% if VIX between 20-24
filters.expiry_filter: skip on RBI policy day, budget day, quarterly expiry

weaknesses: Z-score calculation requires 30+ bars of data, so no trades in first 30 min when volatility is highest
In trending markets, z-score can remain extreme for extended periods — strategy gets stopped out repeatedly
Rolling std denominator is unstable early in session; z-score can give false signals with low sample size
prior_art: Z-score mean reversion is textbook statistical arbitrage (Avellaneda & Lee, 2010). VWAP-specific z-score approaches are common in institutional TWAP/VWAP execution algos. Chan (2013) 'Algorithmic Trading' discusses z-score entry for pairs but same logic applies to VWAP deviation.
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; signal conversion from individual stock to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index; lookback period scaling for 5-second bars; stop/target recalibration for 5-second timeframe. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
